decision_rules.action: Do not persist it — either add at least one real, concrete decision_rule/heuristic or discard the draft entirely
decision_rules.condition: A methodology draft has zero decision_rules and zero heuristics

decision_rules.action: Search existing methodologies by the same keywords first (relevance-filtered, not any-overlap) and only proceed if nothing genuinely covers it already
decision_rules.condition: Before creating a new methodology for a keyword set

decision_rules.action: Rewrite it as a specific 'if X then do Y' before persisting, or drop it
decision_rules.condition: A decision_rule's condition or action is vague or restates the methodology's own keywords rather than describing a concrete, checkable situation and a concrete response

description: Governs how new methodologies get created and how existing ones are reviewed, so the methodology store stays a real, non-duplicated, actionable knowledge base rather than a pile of near-identical or empty-shell entries.

heuristics.description: Prefer extending the existing methodology (add_heuristics/add_principles via Update) over creating a new, duplicate one
heuristics.name: A newly proposed methodology's keyword set overlaps more than half with an existing methodology's keyword set
heuristics.when_to_apply: A newly proposed methodology's keyword set overlaps more than half with an existing methodology's keyword set

name: Methodology Hygiene

principles.rationale: A methodology should cover one coherent, specific concern well rather than being either a vague catch-all or an unnecessary duplicate of an existing one.
A methodology with keywords and a name but no real decision_rules or heuristics is not usable — it must not be persisted as if it were.
